Create a small, polished graph for a synthetic release-readiness walkthrough. Use your normal graph client and finish with graph.submit(interactionNode), the documented terminal authoring submission; do not call recursiveComplete. Do not delegate, invoke controls, browse, use any external service, or modify any files outside your normal graph-authoring workspace.
The response root has exactly two connected nodes: "Launch decision" (clientKey launch-decision) and "Evidence shelf" (clientKey evidence-shelf). Launch decision's semantic detail is exactly "Release when error rate stays below 1% and rollback is ready." Its compiled Node Detail presents this concise decision in a clean layout and exposes one real invoke control labeled "Draft rollout recommendation". The invoke instruction asks for a rollout recommendation; author the control without invoking it.
Evidence shelf has a real Expand control labeled "Inspect baseline" to a child layer with the SAME Launch decision node identity reused alongside one connected node titled "Traffic baseline". Do not clone Launch decision. The original invoke must remain usable in both occurrences. Give every node/layer/action a stable clientKey. Compile Node Details using supported graph-client APIs, use clear typography and restrained color, and set Launch decision as the default node of both layers. This is a synthetic fixture with no real customer data; do not invent external facts.
